enhancement.definition: These provisions provide the principal statutory rules on monetary compensation following breach, stipulated sums and rightful rescission.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Section 73 provides compensation for loss or damage naturally arising in the usual course from breach or within the parties’ contemplation when contracting, subject to mitigation principles; section 74 regulates reasonable compensation where a sum or penalty is stipulated; section 75 gives compensation to a party who rightfully rescinds.
essentialIngredients: Establish a valid contract and breach or rightful rescission.
For section 73, identify loss arising naturally or within contemplated special circumstances and exclude remote loss.
For section 74, identify the stipulated sum or penalty and assess reasonable compensation within the statutory ceiling.
For section 75, establish that rescission was rightful and identify the resulting damage.
enhancement.detailedExplanation:
India Code rule: Section 73 provides compensation for loss or damage naturally arising in the usual course from breach or within the parties’ contemplation when contracting, subject to mitigation principles; section 74 regulates reasonable compensation where a sum or penalty is stipulated; section 75 gives compensation to a party who rightfully rescinds.

Definition: These provisions provide the principal statutory rules on monetary compensation following breach, stipulated sums and rightful rescission.

Ingredients:
1. Establish a valid contract and breach or rightful rescission.
2. For section 73, identify loss arising naturally or within contemplated special circumstances and exclude remote loss.
3. For section 74, identify the stipulated sum or penalty and assess reasonable compensation within the statutory ceiling.
4. For section 75, establish that rescission was rightful and identify the resulting damage.
examples: A contracts to sing for two nights each week for two months but wilfully misses a performance and B rightfully rescinds; the section 75 illustration recognises compensation for damage caused by non-fulfilment.
problemApplication: Apply sections 73–75: identify the guarantee/indemnity relationship, test the statutory condition or discharge rule, address the opposing position, and state the consequence.
keyTakeaways: Section 73 provides compensation for loss or damage naturally arising in the usual course from breach or within the parties’ contemplation when contracting, subject to mitigation principles; section 74 regulates reasonable compensation where a sum or penalty is stipulated; section 75 gives compensation to a party who rightfully rescinds.
These provisions provide the principal statutory rules on monetary compensation following breach, stipulated sums and rightful rescission.
